resources.string: Published 20/40/80 m designs, wire cut lists and trap calculations.

A trap is a parallel LC circuit inserted into a dipole arm. At its resonant frequency it presents a high impedance, so very little current flows in the wire beyond the trap and that section contributes little to the antenna’s operation. Below resonance the trap acts like an inductor and electrically lengthens the arm. Above resonance it acts like a capacitor and electrically shortens it. This lets one centre-fed wire work on several bands without a tuner or a frequency-selective feed line.

• The classic W3DZZ, also known as G8KW, uses traps near 7.1 MHz. The centre section is a half-wave dipole on 40 m. On 80 m the full wire works with the traps as loading coils. On 20, 15 and 10 m the full wire operates near harmonic resonances (1.5λ, 2.5λ and 3.5λ).
• A dedicated two-band design such as 80/40 m or 40/20 m can be tuned directly on both bands. The higher harmonic bands of W3DZZ are a compromise.
• On 80 m the shortened antenna has a narrow SWR bandwidth, typically about 100–200 kHz.
• On 20, 40 and 80 m the feed point is near a current maximum in the middle of the radiator. A current choke helps suppress common-mode feed-line current.
• For 20/40/80 m, use W3DZZ with 7 MHz traps and harmonic operation on 20 m, or use a purpose-built dipole with 20 m and 40 m traps in each arm.
Resonance, SWR bandwidth and the need for a tuner depend on the installed antenna. R2AUK measured about 160 kHz on 80 m at SWR below 2.
